body.statement:
Let \(G^{(4)}=(V,D,B)\) have \(V=\{0,1,2,3,4\}\),
\[
 D=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,2\to3,1\to4,2\to4\},
 \qquad
 B=\{0\leftrightarrow i:1\leq i\leq4\},
\]
let
\[
 T=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,1\to4\},
 \qquad e=2\to4,
\]
and write \(f=\lambda_e\). Then \((G^{(4)},T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\) and \(d_e(G^{(4)})=4\). More precisely, at the rational positive-definite covariance \(\Sigma^{\star}\) displayed in the proof, the residual fiber has four reduced points with distinct real \(f\)-coordinates, namely the roots of
\[
 q(f)=(f-7)\bigl(8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
 +1271943861499f-2976933819575\bigr).
\]
Every root extends to real directed coefficients and a positive-definite disturbance matrix \(\Omega\) having the required missing-bidirected zero pattern. For every \(N\geq5\), appending \(N-5\) fully bidirected children of \(0\) and placing their arrows in \(T\) preserves the queried-coordinate degree four. Consequently \(D_k(5)\geq4\) for every admissible \(k\geq2\).
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 (a,b,c,d,u,f)=(\lambda_{01},\lambda_{02},\lambda_{13},
 \lambda_{23},\lambda_{14},\lambda_{24}).
\]
The displayed \(T\) has four arrows, gives every nonroot exactly one parent, and reaches every vertex from \(0\); hence it is a rooted spanning arborescence.  Moreover
\[
 D\setminus T=\{2\to3,2\to4\},
\]
the order \(0<1<2<3<4\) is topological, and \(e=2\to4\).  Therefore \((G^{(4)},T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\) by \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\).

At the rational source point
\[
 (a,b,c,d,u,f)=(2,3,4,5,6,7),
 \qquad
 \Omega^\star=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 30&1&2&3&4\\
 1&31&0&0&0\\
 2&0&32&0&0\\
 3&0&0&33&0\\
 4&0&0&0&34
 \end{pmatrix},
\tag{77}
\]
all nonzero off-diagonal disturbance entries are allowed by \(B\).  The inequality \(2|y_iy_j|\le y_i^2+y_j^2\) gives, for \(y\ne0\),
\[
 y^{\mathsf T}\Omega^\star y
 \ge20y_0^2+30y_1^2+30y_2^2+30y_3^2+30y_4^2>0,
\]
so \(\Omega^\star\succ0\).  Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \Sigma^\star=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 30&61&92&707&1014\\
 61&155&187&1561&2247\\
 92&187&314&2327&3332\\
 707&1561&2327&17981&25747\\
 1014&2247&3332&25747&36972
 \end{pmatrix}.
\tag{78}
\]
It is positive definite by congruence because \(I_5-\Lambda^\star\) is unit triangular.

The missing bidirected pairs are the six pairs inside \(\{1,2,3,4\}\).  Substitution into their residuals gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_1={}&30ab-92a-61b+187,\\
 R_2={}&61ac+92ad-707a-155c-187d+1561,\\
 R_3={}&61au+92af-1014a-155u-187f+2247,\\
 R_4={}&61bc+92bd-707b-187c-314d+2327,\\
 R_5={}&61bu+92bf-1014b-187u-314f+3332,\\
 R_6={}&155cu+187cf-2247c+187du+314df-3332d\\
 &{}-1561u-2327f+25747.
\end{aligned}
\tag{79}
\]
Exact Buchberger reduction over \(\mathbb Q\), in lexicographic order \(a>b>c>d>u>f\), gives the following triangular basis, with harmless nonzero rational normalizations suppressed:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 H_1={}&384915840a+425450175590061f^3-8965411803407607f^2\\
 &{}+62974399432228195f-147445028655847225,\\
 H_2={}&741827520b-593375419233f^3+12321625507347f^2\\
 &{}-85271405126447f+196665729339485,\\
 H_3={}&615040c+25798931271f^3-543666188277f^2\\
 &{}+3818873142057f-8941504654939,\\
 H_4={}&4d-3f+1,\\
 H_5={}&153760u+8599643757f^3-181222062759f^2\\
 &{}+1272957714019f-2980501654153,\\
 H_6={}&q(f)=(f-7)c(f),\\
 c(f)={}&8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
 +1271943861499f-2976933819575.
\end{aligned}
\tag{80}
\]
This is a two-sided exact ideal certificate.  Each \(H_j\) is obtained from the \(R_i\) by rational \(S\)-polynomial reductions, and division of every \(R_i\) by \((H_1,\ldots,H_6)\) has zero remainder.  Conversely, the leading monomials of the normalized \(H_j\) are \(a,b,c,d,u,f^4\), which are pairwise relatively prime; Buchberger's product criterion makes all remaining \(S\)-polynomials reduce to zero.  Thus the reductions certify
\[
 (R_1,\ldots,R_6)=(H_1,\ldots,H_6)
\tag{81}
\]
over characteristic zero, not merely modulo a prime.

Exact integer arithmetic gives
\[
 c(7)=-30256,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{disc}(c)
 =1802165059445823134111101206528>0.
\tag{82}
\]
A real cubic with one real root and a nonreal pair \(s\pm it\), \(t\ne0\), has discriminant
\[
 -4A^4t^2\bigl((r-s)^2+t^2\bigr)^2<0,
\]
where \(A\) is its leading coefficient.  Thus the positive discriminant in (82) gives three distinct real roots of \(c\), and \(c(7)\ne0\) excludes \(7\).  Hence \(q\) has four distinct real roots.  The first five equations in (80) recover a unique real \((a,b,c,d,u)\) from each root, so (81) yields
\[
 \mathbb C[a,b,c,d,u,f]/(R_1,\ldots,R_6)
 \cong\mathbb C[f]/(q)\cong\mathbb C^4.
\tag{83}
\]
Thus the specialized residual fiber is reduced and its four \(f\)-coordinates are distinct.

The residual Jacobian has rank six at all four points.  Indeed, the triangular Jacobian has the five displayed nonzero constant derivatives and last derivative \(q'(f)\ne0\); differentiating the two-sided identities in (81) identifies its row span with that of the original residual Jacobian.  Perturb the fifteen covariance entries independently as \(\Sigma^\star+z\).  The invertible Jacobian recursively solves the degree-\(r\) equation for a formal directed-coordinate series at every point, producing four formal branches with distinct constant \(f\)-terms.

The source dimension is
\[
 |D|+|B|+|V|=6+4+5=15,
\tag{84}
\]
equal to the covariance dimension.  A full-rank formal section makes the covariance parametrization dominant: a covariance polynomial in its kernel vanishes after the injective translation \(\Sigma^\star+z\), and hence is zero.  Thus \(P_G=(0)\), \(K_G=\mathbb C(\sigma_{ij}:i\le j)\), and \(L/K_G\) is finite.

Partition the directed variables into the four incoming-vertex blocks \(A=(a)\), \(B_0=(b)\), \(C=(c,d)\), and \(U_0=(u,f)\).  The six residuals have binary graph \(K_4\) and degree at most one in each incident block.  Therefore
\[
 [L:K_G]\le
 [AB_0C^2U_0^2]
 (A+B_0)(A+C)(A+U_0)(B_0+C)(B_0+U_0)(C+U_0)=4
\tag{85}
\]
by the multihomogeneous lemma and the small-block count.  The four formal branches give four distinct roots of the original-coordinate minimal polynomial, so
\[
 4\le[K_G(f):K_G]\le[L:K_G]\le4.
\tag{86}
\]
Thus \(d_e(G^{(4)})=4\).

For every root, let \(\widetilde\Lambda\) be its real triangular recovery and set
\[
 \widetilde\Omega=(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}
 \Sigma^\star(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda).
\]
Equations (79) are exactly the six entries required to vanish, so the support is correct.  Acyclicity makes \(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda\) unit triangular and invertible; \(\Sigma^\star\succ0\) and congruence give \(\widetilde\Omega\succ0\).  Hence all four roots have real supported positive-definite lifts.

Finally append a new child \(w\) of \(0\), put its arrow in \(T\), and allow every bidirected pair incident with \(w\).  No new missing residual involves \(w\).  Congruence is an invertible triangular change between the new allowed disturbance row and the new covariance row \(s_w\), so
\[
 L_1=L_0(\lambda_{0w},s_w),\qquad K_1=K_0(s_w),
\]
with the adjoined variables algebraically independent.  Purely transcendental base extension preserves the old minimal polynomial's irreducibility and therefore its degree four.  Iteration proves the appending claim.  Since \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\subseteq\mathcal G_{5,k}\) for admissible \(k\ge2\), the definition of \(D_k(5)\) gives the final lower bound.
